summary: Creates a closed 3D polygonal surface around pixels or points that exceed a threshold, using either a 3D texture TOP or a 3-dimensional POP grid as input.

key_params.name: top
key_params.note: 3D texture TOP input when using texture input

key_params.name: inputattrscope
key_params.note: Attribute sampled from a 3D POP grid

key_params.name: posattrib
key_params.note: Use P attribute to position surface when using POP input

key_params.name: resmult
key_params.note: Resolution multiplier to reduce output density

key_params.name: inside
key_params.note: Choose signed-distance or density inside test and winding orientation

key_params.name: uniquepoints
key_params.note: Create unique points per triangle instead of shared points

key_params.name: tolow
key_params.note: Low XYZ target range for P re-range

key_params.name: tohigh
key_params.note: High XYZ target range for P re-range

key_params.name: nmlstepmul
key_params.note: Field-gradient step multiplier for normal computation

key_params.name: allocfract
key_params.note: Fraction of maximum GPU allocation to reserve

key_params.name: cpureadback
key_params.note: Copy topology information back to the CPU

key_concepts: Polygonize POP extracts a closed 3D surface from a thresholded 3D texture or a 3-dimensional POP grid.
Inside mode, threshold, extend mode, and channel selection determine which sampled field values become surface triangles and how they are wound.
Allocation fraction, unique/shared points, P re-range, normals, texture coordinates, and CPU readback control output density, placement, shading, and diagnostics.
common_gotchas: Current docs describe this as a 3D polygonization path; use Trace POP for 2D contour workflows.
A POP input must be arranged as a 3-dimensional grid.
3D texture input assumes cube-like pixels and outputs P(0) in a default -.5 to .5 range unless re-ranged.
